portName: Melville Street Cruise Terminal, St George's
seoTitle: Grenada cruise port guide: St George's, Carenage, Grand Anse
seoDescription: Ships dock at Melville Street, in St George's town. Walk to the Carenage; water taxi to Grand Anse US$5 or Route 1 minibus EC$2.50–6.50 range (2026).
quickAnswer: Large ships dock at the Melville Street Cruise Terminal and you walk straight through the Esplanade Mall into St George's, so the town, the market and the Carenage need no transport. For Grand Anse beach take a water taxi from the Carenage (about US$5 one way, about 10 minutes) or a Route 1 minibus. Be back at the ship 60 minutes before all-aboard, and 90 minutes before if you are relying on a minibus.
intro: St George's is a steep harbour town built around a horseshoe bay, and the cruise berth sits right on its edge. You step off the ship, cross the Esplanade Mall and you are in town. The Carenage waterfront curves round the inner harbour on the other side of the Fort George headland, linked by the Sendall Tunnel and the streets over the hill. Most visitors split the day between the town and two miles of sand at Grand Anse, a short boat or minibus ride south. Allow for hills, heat and afternoon traffic on the road back.
tenderNotes: Large ships berth at the Melville Street Cruise Terminal. Smaller ships and yachts can use the inner harbour at the Carenage. On busy days, when more ships are in port than the berths can take, extra ships anchor off the town and tender passengers ashore along the Carenage.

terminals.name: Melville Street Cruise Terminal
terminals.notes: On the edge of the town centre, just north of Fort George. Passengers walk through the Esplanade Mall into St George's. The town bus terminal, where minibuses and taxis gather, is about 200 yards north of the cruise terminal.

terminals.name: Carenage (inner harbour)
terminals.notes: Used by smaller ships and by tenders on busy days. Water taxis to Grand Anse leave from the Carenage.

walkability.detail: The town starts at the terminal. Bruce Street, the market area and the Carenage are within walking distance, but St George's is hilly, with steep streets, steps and pavements that sometimes disappear mid-block. Walkers are better off crossing the headland by Young Street than walking through the narrow, poorly ventilated Sendall Tunnel. Fort George is a short but steep climb.

transportSections.time: Town centre straight from the terminal
transportSections.detail: Exit through the Esplanade Mall onto Bruce Street. For the Carenage, go over the hill via Young Street. Traffic drives on the left.

transportSections.cost: About US$5 per person one way (2026); price depends on the operator
transportSections.detail: Boats leave from the Carenage. Agree the fare and the return pick-up time with the skipper before boarding. Carry small US notes.

transportSections.cost: Minibus fares EC$2.50–6.50 depending on route (2026); cash only
transportSections.detail: Minibuses gather at the bus terminal about 200 yards north of the cruise terminal; the route number is shown on the windscreen. Buses run 06:00–21:00 Monday to Saturday. They can be crowded, and drivers often speed.

transportSections.cost: Unmetered; agree the fare and currency before setting off
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait near the terminal and at the bus station. Use only licensed taxis. Fares can usually be paid in US or Eastern Caribbean dollars.

returnTiming.rule: Be back at the ship 60 minutes before all-aboard. Leave Grand Anse 90 minutes before all-aboard, and be back from Annandale Falls or a sculpture-park boat trip 2 hours before.
returnTiming.detail: The road between Grand Anse and St George's backs up in afternoon traffic, and minibuses fill with commuters. The water taxi avoids the road but depends on your skipper coming back on time, so agree a pick-up well before you need it.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If the boat does not come, take a taxi from the Grand Anse road back to the Melville Street terminal; it is about 15 minutes in normal traffic. If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme straight away.

excursionAdvice: You do not need a tour for St George's or Grand Anse: the town starts at the gangway and the beach is a short boat ride away. A ship tour makes sense for the interior, such as Grand Etang, the spice estates and the rum and chocolate producers, where roads are narrow and winding and a private return has no guarantee. For the Underwater Sculpture Park you need a boat either way; a ship-sold trip removes the return risk, a local operator is usually cheaper.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 and all-aboard is 16:30 for a 17:00 sailing.

steps.what: Walk off through the Esplanade Mall into St George's. Head over the hill on Young Street to the Carenage.
Walk the Carenage waterfront to the Christ of the Deep statue. Stop at the House of Chocolate for a demonstration and samples.
Climb to Fort George for the view over the harbour, or use the viewing platform near the police headquarters if the fort is closed.
Browse the market for nutmeg and other spices (busiest on Saturday). Bring small notes.
Water taxi from the Carenage to Grand Anse. Agree the return pick-up time before you step off.
Swim and lunch at Grand Anse; the Craft and Spice Market is on the beach.
Water taxi back to the Carenage, leaving Grand Anse no later than 15:00.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: The Carenage
sights.why: The horseshoe-shaped inner harbour with fishing boats, bars and the Christ of the Deep statue.
sights.tip: Water taxis to Grand Anse leave from here.

sights.name: Fort George
sights.why: French-built fort of 1706–1710 above the harbour mouth, with cannons, barracks and the best view over the town and bay.
sights.cost: Small fee when open; check on the day
sights.tip: A short, steep climb from town. If it is closed, a viewing platform up the steps opposite the police headquarters gives a similar view.

sights.name: Grenada National Museum
sights.why: Housed in one of the island's oldest buildings, at Young and Monckton Streets, once the colonial constabulary and later a hotel; the collection includes a rum still.
sights.tip: Check it is open before you go: call 473 440 3725.

sights.name: St George's market
sights.why: Stalls of nutmeg, mace, cinnamon and other spices, plus produce, in the centre of town.
sights.tip: Saturday is busiest, with the most vendors. Spices here are better value than at stalls near the gangway.

sights.name: House of Chocolate
sights.why: Grenadian chocolate shop and small museum by the Carenage with bean-to-bar demonstrations, samples and ice cream.
sights.tip: A cool stop in the midday heat.

sights.name: St George's Roman Catholic Cathedral and Church Street
sights.why: The hillside streets above the Carenage, with the cathedral, the Anglican church ruins and the old town houses.
sights.tip: Steep steps and lanes; be quiet if a service is on.

sights.name: Annandale Falls
sights.why: Waterfall and pool in the hills, about 20 minutes' drive from town and a five-minute walk from the car park.
sights.tip: A man jumps from the cliff for visitors and asks for money afterwards; decide beforehand whether you want to pay.

sights.name: Underwater Sculpture Park (Molinere Bay)
sights.why: Sculptures on the seabed in about 16 feet of water, seen by snorkelling or diving.
sights.cost: Tours about US$55–100 per person; marine park wristband US$1 snorkel, US$2 dive (2026)
sights.tip: Not reachable on foot from the berth. Book a tour that guarantees a return in time.

beaches.name: Grand Anse
beaches.howToGetThere: Water taxi from the Carenage, Route 1 minibus or taxi
beaches.time: 5–10 minutes by water taxi, 20–30 minutes by minibus, about 15 minutes by taxi
beaches.cost: Water taxi about US$5 each way (2026); beach free
beaches.note: Two miles of white sand with hotels, beach bars, water sports and a Craft and Spice Market. Not all beaches have lifeguards; ask locally before swimming.

commonMistakes.fix: Camouflage is illegal for visitors in Grenada and can be confiscated. Leave it on the ship or at home.
It is narrow and poorly ventilated, with traffic. Cross the headland on Young Street instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving Grand Anse at the last minute.
commonMistakes.fix: The road back jams in the afternoon. Leave 90 minutes before all-aboard and fix the water taxi pick-up in advance.

commonMistakes.mistake: Getting into a taxi without agreeing the fare.
commonMistakes.fix: Taxis are unmetered. Agree the price, and whether it is in US or EC dollars, before you get in.

commonMistakes.mistake: Relying on minibuses on a Sunday.
commonMistakes.fix: Minibuses run Monday to Saturday. On Sundays use the water taxi or a taxi.

safety: The US State Department rates Grenada Level 2 (exercise increased caution) because of crime, and the UK says most crime is non-violent and opportunistic. Daytime visits to St George's and Grand Anse are routine, but keep valuables out of sight, do not carry much cash or jewellery, and do not leave drinks unattended. Currents can be strong and not all beaches have lifeguards or flags, so ask locally before swimming. Minibus drivers often speed. Hurricane season runs from June to November. Check the alert level for Kick 'em Jenny, the underwater volcano about 5 miles off the coast, if your plans include boat trips.
scams: Taxi fare disputes: taxis are unmetered, so confirm the price and currency before you get in, and use licensed taxis only.
Pay-after-the-show at Annandale Falls: a cliff jumper performs and then asks visitors for money; agree beforehand whether you will tip.
accessibility: The berth and the Esplanade Mall are on the flat at the harbour edge, but St George's is built on steep hills with steps and gaps in the pavement. The Carenage waterfront is mostly level once you reach it, but the way over the headland is steep; a taxi round to the Carenage is easier for wheelchair users. Fort George and the upper town are not suitable for wheelchairs. Minibuses are not accessible. Grand Anse has a long, gently shelving beach; ask about water-taxi boarding before you go.
rainyDay: Showers are usually short. Spend the time in the House of Chocolate, the National Museum (check it is open) and the cafés along the Carenage. Skip the steep climb to Fort George in heavy rain, as the streets get slippery, and avoid rivers and waterfalls after heavy rain.
crowdTips: The season's busiest months are December to February, with around 40 calls a month in 2026–27. When two or more large ships are in, the Esplanade Mall and the water taxis at the Carenage get busy straight after arrival. See the Carenage and Fort George early, go to Grand Anse late morning, and come back before the afternoon traffic.

faqs.a: Usually not. Large ships dock at the Melville Street Cruise Terminal in St George's. On very busy days extra ships anchor and tender to the Carenage.

faqs.q: Is St George's walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. You walk through the Esplanade Mall straight into town. The streets are steep in places.

faqs.q: How do I get from Grenada cruise port to Grand Anse beach?
faqs.a: Water taxi from the Carenage, about US$5 one way and 5–10 minutes, or a Route 1 minibus from the bus terminal near the berth, about 20–30 minutes.

faqs.q: How do I get from the cruise terminal to the Carenage?
faqs.a: Walk over the headland via Young Street. Avoid walking through the Sendall Tunnel.

faqs.q: What can I do in Grenada in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk the Carenage, climb to Fort George, buy spices at the market, then spend the afternoon at Grand Anse.

faqs.q: Can I use US dollars in Grenada?
faqs.a: Yes, widely, but change often comes in Eastern Caribbean dollars. Carry small US notes; minibuses take cash only.

faqs.q: Is Grenada safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Generally yes in daytime. The US advises increased caution because of crime; keep valuables out of sight and agree taxi fares first.
